authority: Cambridge International AS & A Level Computer Science 9618 syllabus, 2027-2029, Version 2

records.resolution: Directly compares redundancy, inconsistency, isolation, incompatible formats, duplicated controls and difficult shared access/backup in file-based systems with the specific relational or DBMS mechanisms that address each limitation.
Teaches all Version 2 relational terms, all three relationship cardinalities, referential integrity and indexing; candidate, primary, secondary and foreign keys have separate definitions.
Requires students to produce and interpret an E-R diagram using entities, relationships and cardinality, including a linking entity for many-to-many designs.
Defines 1NF, 2NF and 3NF precisely, distinguishes partial and transitive dependencies, and requires a normalised design that preserves facts, keys and relationships.
Covers data management and dictionary, data modelling, logical schema, integrity, security, backup/recovery and individual/group access rights as distinct DBMS features.
Distinguishes the developer interface used to define/build database applications from the query processor that interprets, checks and carries out statements.
Separates DDL structure creation/modification from DML querying/data maintenance and identifies SQL as the industry-standard language used for both.
Teaches students to explain the effect of a complete SQL statement through its clauses, identifiers, operators, literal values and result, rather than recognise isolated keywords.
Covers CREATE DATABASE, CREATE TABLE, ALTER TABLE, all seven required data types, and primary/foreign key clauses with REFERENCES.
Covers every required retrieval, ordering, grouping, aggregate and join construct while enforcing the AS boundary of at most two tables and explicit INNER JOIN ... ON syntax.
Directly teaches and assesses INSERT INTO, UPDATE and DELETE FROM, including the role of WHERE when only selected records should change.
Removes the false secondary/alternate-key equivalence throughout maintained teaching and assessment data; a secondary key is now an additional retrieval field that need not be unique.

Replaces the three-table comma-style Section 8 review question and mark scheme with an explicit two-table Student INNER JOIN Loan ON query and separate WHERE condition, without changing its six marks.
Replaces the dependency-losing normalisation infographic with a deterministic 1536x1024 visual that states 1NF, 2NF and 3NF in order and preserves facts, keys and relationships.
Removes the Access-specific #date# literal from core SQL and uses the course's quoted date style so the example is consistent with the industry-standard SQL boundary taught elsewhere.
